title: Sections of a constant etale sheaf are locally constant maps
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an abelian group, and let $\underline E$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the constant presheaf $U\mapsto E$ on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], i.e. the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A map $f:|T|\to E$ is *Zariski-locally constant* if every point $x\in|T|$ has a Zariski-open neighbourhood $V$ on which $f$ is constant; equivalently, every fibre $f^{-1}(\{e\})$ is Zariski open (the converse follows because an arbitrary fibre is the union of the open neighbourhoods on which $f$ has value $e$). Let $\operatorname{LC}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(|T|,E)$ be the abelian group of such maps, with pointwise addition. Then, by the Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5), using the representability input Lemma 59.15.8 (Tag 03O3), there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups $\underline E(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{LC}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(|T|,E)$ taking the section $\iota_T(e)$ induced by $e\in E$ to the constant map with value $e$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5, label etale-cohomology-remark-constant-locally-constant-maps): the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value a group G has Gamma(U, G) equal to the Zariski-locally-constant maps U -> G. The remark identifies the Zariski sheafification with the representable constant group scheme of Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW), and uses Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.15.8 (Tag 03O3), that representable presheaves satisfy the fpqc sheaf condition.

proof.text: Equip E with the discrete topology and define L(U)=LocallyConstant(|U|,E), with pointwise addition and pullback restrictions. Sending a locally constant map to its continuous map gives a natural additive isomorphism with the restriction of the fpqc sheaf U ↦ C(|U|,E) [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf]. An etale covering is fpqc, so this is an etale sheaf; the continuous forgetful functor Scheme.Etale.forget T ⋙ Over.forget T restricts it to the small site. In Lean the fpqc-to-etale topology inequality factors through the pro-etale topology.

source.place: Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5); direct continuous-map proof, using Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/ConstantSheaf.lean and Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallyBijective.lean

proof.text: Define alpha:E_const → L by constant functions. For a section s on an etale object U, its open fibres F_e={x | s(x)=e} are open subschemes, hence etale over T. Their inclusions cover U because x belongs to F_{s(x)}, and the restriction of s to F_e equals the constant e. Thus the image sieve of s is covering, giving local surjectivity. If alpha(a)=alpha(b), either a=b, and their equalizer sieve is top, or evaluating at any point contradicts a≠b. In the latter case U is empty, its empty covering is contained in the equalizer sieve. This gives local injectivity, including the empty scheme.

source.place: Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5); direct continuous-map proof, using Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/ConstantSheaf.lean and Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallyBijective.lean

proof.text: By the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], alpha factors as eta followed by a sheaf morphism c:E_const^# → L. The unit eta is locally bijective and local injectivity and surjectivity cancel across it (Mathlib Presheaf.comp_isLocallyInjective_iff and comp_isLocallySurjective_iff). Hence c is locally bijective, so it is an isomorphism by the concrete sheaf local-bijectivity criterion in Mathlib, equivalently [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective]. Evaluate this isomorphism at Etale.mk (𝟙 T) and take its additive equivalence. Evaluating eta ≫ c = alpha at e proves exactly that the canonical section e maps to LocallyConstant.const T e.
